title: Finite normalization of a semilinear projective modification
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be a normal integral proper finite-type $k$-scheme, and let $T$ be an integral finite-type $k$-scheme projective over $k$. Let a finite group $H$ act semilinearly on $T$, $X$ and $k$, and let $p:T\to X$ be an equivariant $k$-morphism inducing an isomorphism $k(X)\simeq k(T)$. Assume there is a dense open $U\subseteq X$ over which $p$ is an isomorphism. Let $n:N\to T$ be the normalization of $T$ in $k(T)$. Then $n$ is finite, surjective and birational, $N$ is normal integral of finite type and projective over $k$, and the given action on $T$ lifts uniquely to a semilinear $H$-action on $N$ making $n$ equivariant. The composite $p n:N\to X$ is equivariant, proper, surjective and H-projective, induces the specified identification $k(X)\simeq k(N)$, and is an isomorphism over $U$. If $X$ is geometrically integral over $k$, then $T$ and $N$ are geometrically integral over $k$ as well.

The notions used are [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-kun-projective], [def-sc-function-field], [def-sc-normalization], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-weil-open-immersion], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. A projective morphism here means an H-projective morphism: it admits a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over its target. A semilinear $H$-action means actions by scheme automorphisms and by field automorphisms of $k$, with the structure morphisms equivariant; faithfulness is not assumed. A birational morphism here identifies the function fields and is an isomorphism over a dense open of the target.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-normalization-model-functoriality] with $V=T$, $M=H=k(T)$ and the identity field extension (here its letter $H$ denotes the function field, not our group). It gives normal integral finite-type $N$, finite surjective $n$, and the canonical identification $k(N)=k(T)$. Independently [lem-sc-normalization-exists] gives birationality of $n$. Composing the canonical field identification with the specified $p^*:k(X)\simeq k(T)$ gives exactly $(pn)^*:k(X)\simeq k(N)$.

A field is Noetherian: its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$, so every ideal is finitely generated. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is affine Noetherian. The structure map $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is H-projective by hypothesis and quasi-compact because it is of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], so it is projective in the convention required by the next cited statement. Apply [lem-fin-finite-over-projective] to $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the finite map $n:N\to T$. Its affine-base clause gives a closed immersion $N\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^r_k$ for a finite $r$, proving projectivity in the required finite-projective-space convention.

source.place: Tag 0GK4, lemma-normalize-projective; morphisms.tex Tags 0B3I, lemma-finite-projective, and 087S, lemma-projective-over-quasi-projective-is-H-projective.

proof.text: For each $h\in H$ use its scheme automorphism of $T$, its field automorphism of $k$, and its induced automorphism of $k(T)$ in the semilinear-isomorphism clause of [lem-sfb-finite-normalization-model-functoriality]. This gives a unique compatible automorphism $\widetilde h$ of $N$. Preservation of identities and compositions gives $\widetilde 1=1$ and $\widetilde{h_1h_2}=\widetilde h_1\widetilde h_2$. The lifts commute with $n$ and have the original semilinearity on $k$. Hence $pn$ is equivariant. Any other equivariant lift induces the same automorphism on $k(N)=k(T)$, so the uniqueness clause forces equality. Faithfulness and invariance of the specified open $U$ are unnecessary.

source.place: Tag 035Q, lemma-normalization-normal (4); explicit semilinear functoriality of the integral-closure construction.

proof.text: Put $V=p^{-1}(U)$. The given isomorphism $V\simeq U$ identifies local rings, and the local rings of $U$ are those of the normal scheme $X$. Thus $V$ is normal. By [lem-sc-normalization-over-normal-locus], $n^{-1}(V)\to V$ is an isomorphism. Composing it with $V\simeq U$ proves that $pn$ is an isomorphism over the original $U$.

By [def-weil-proper-morphism], $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated, and $pn:N\to X$ is a $k$-morphism. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-constant-projective-graph] with $F=k$ (the trivial finite extension), $R=N$, which embeds as a closed subscheme of $\mathbf P^r_k$ by step 2, $S=X$ and $c=pn$. It gives an integer $N'\geq0$ and a closed immersion $(i,pn):N\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{N'}_k\times_kX\cong\mathbf P^{N'}_X$ over $X$: precisely H-projectivity of $pn$ in the finite-projective-space convention, with no equivariant-embedding assertion. By [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], $pn$ is proper. Its image is closed by [def-weil-proper-morphism] and contains the dense open $U$ by step 4, hence is all of $X$. This proves surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 0C4Q, lemma-projective-permanence, closed-graph proof (as stated in the cited node); Tag 01WC, lemma-locally-projective-proper.

proof.text: Assume $X$ geometrically integral. Choose a nonempty affine open $A\subset X$. By [lem-zl-geometric-irreducibility-affine-local] it is geometrically irreducible. It is geometrically reduced because for every extension $L/k$, $A_L$ is open in reduced $X_L$, and its local rings are those of $X_L$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. For $Y=T$ or $N$ and every nonempty affine open $B\subset Y$, [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] identifies the fraction fields of the section rings of $A$ and $B$ with $k(X)$ and $k(Y)$. Compose these fraction-field identifications with $p^*$ and, for $Y=N$, $n^*$. Because $p,n$ are $k$-morphisms, the resulting ring equivalence fixes every base section, as required by the next cited statement. Therefore [lem-sbc-field-fraction-ring-geometric-integrality] applies to $A,B$ and proves that every such $B$ is geometrically irreducible and geometrically reduced.

source.place: Tags 038G, lemma-geometrically-irreducible-local; 035W, lemma-geometrically-reduced-at-point; 054Q, lemma-geometrically-irreducible-function-field. Affine fraction-field transfer as in the cited node.

proof.text: For each $Y=T,N$, integrality gives irreducibility. The affine-local equivalence in [lem-zl-geometric-irreducibility-affine-local], applied to step 6, proves geometric irreducibility of $Y$. For every $L/k$, the base changes of its affine opens cover $Y_L$ and are reduced by step 6. Every local ring of $Y_L$ is a local ring of one of these opens, hence reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Thus $Y_L$ is both irreducible and reduced, and therefore integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Since $L$ was arbitrary, both $T$ and $N$ are geometrically integral [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].

source.place: Tags 038G, lemma-geometrically-irreducible-local, and 038K, lemma-geometrically-integral; reducedness is local by its definition.
